messages:
ryan_customer: Hey team — after we switched the service to use a VPCE + NLB in front of our ALB, clients in the VPC are intermittently getting 502s and big tail latency (~4-6s) to /v1/generate. Public traffic is fine. @support_julia can you help?

support_julia: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the VPCE id, region, and an example request/response (headers) for a failing call? Also any recent infra changes?

ryan_customer: VPCE vpce-0a1b2c3d, us-east-1. We did a cutover to an NLB (zonal) that fronts an internal ALB. NLB listener is TLS (443) with cert, then re-encrypts to ALB on 8443. Example curl (from inside client subnet):

```
> curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://inference.internal/v1/generate
* Connected to inference.internal (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.internal
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-length: 0
< x-request-id: abc123
```

It succeeds from a public test host. Failures are only from VPC via the interface endpoint.

infra_oncall_mark: Can you share NLB/ALB health check config and describe-target-health output? 502s often come from target failures or host-based routing mismatches. Also confirm SG/NACLs allow ephemeral ports.

ryan_customer: Health checks look fine most of the time, but targets do briefly report UNHEALTHY then go back to healthy. Snip from describe-target-health (sanitized):

```
TargetDescription: 10.0.3.45:8443 -> healthy(3/3) / unhealthy(1/3 intermittently)
TargetDescription: 10.0.4.12:8443 -> healthy
```

We double-checked SGs: ALB SG allows 8443 from NLB SG, NLB SG allows 443 from interface endpoint. NACLs are default allow.

devx_amy: Two things to check quickly: 1) Is the NLB doing TLS termination? If so it will strip SNI when it terminates and the backend ALB might be using SNI for host-based routing / cert selection. 2) Are you using proxy protocol? That can change client IP behavior and backend cert selection in some setups. Our runtime uses SNI to select the model pool in a few cases.

ryan_customer: We are using TLS listener on the NLB (cert attached) and re-encrypting to the ALB. Interesting note — tcpdump on the backend shows occasional ClientHello without SNI when the request comes via the VPCE. Example tcpdump excerpt (base64 redacted):

```
12:01:13.123 IP 10.0.5.22.52344 > 10.0.3.45.8443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1
TLS ClientHello (no SNI)
---
12:01:13.456 IP 10.0.5.22.52344 > 10.0.3.45.8443: TLS ClientHello (SNI: inference.internal)
```

So sometimes SNI present, sometimes not. When no SNI, ALB returns 502 (no matching host/cert).

support_julia: That matches a TLS termination symptom. If NLB terminates TLS, the backend connection is a new TLS session between NLB and ALB; to preserve client SNI you need NLB in TCP mode (passthrough) rather than TLS-terminating mode. With TLS listener on NLB the ALB won't consistently see the original client SNI — explained here: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-troubleshooting.html#tls-termination-sni.

Recommendation: switch the NLB listener from TLS -> TCP (passthrough) so the ALB/your backend sees client ClientHello with SNI, or alternatively terminate TLS on the NLB and configure host routing and certs on NLB to match backend expectations. Quick commands to test change (one AZ/canary first):

```
# create TCP listener on NLB targeting the same TG
aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn <nlb-arn> --protocol TCP --port 443 --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=<tg-arn>
# then remove TLS listener once canary healthy
aws elbv2 delete-listener --listener-arn <old-tls-listener-arn>
```

Also double-check ALB target group type (ip vs instance) and preserve client IP settings if you rely on source-based routing.

ryan_customer: Switched the NLB to TCP listener in a single AZ canary — failures disappeared for that AZ within minutes. Rolling out to remaining AZs now. Thanks! :tada:

deploy-bot: Rolling update: nlb-listener-mode -> TCP, region us-east-1. 1/3 AZs updated (canary). No errors reported.

ryan_customer: After full roll our error rate dropped to baseline. Looks good. We also opened a change to document our VPCE + NLB pattern to avoid TLS-termination in front of ALB; will keep an eye.

support_julia: Great — closing this thread. If it reappears please ping and include tcpdump + target health windows. :white_check_mark:
